Elena, Sergio —

I've completed the SSO/SCIM/RBAC sections in the spreadsheet (attached in-line). Summary of the key points here for quick reference:

SSO (SAML/OIDC)
- Supported flows: SAML 2.0 (IdP-initiated & SP-initiated), OIDC Authorization Code + PKCE for web/native flows.
- IdP integrations: We have certified integrations with Okta, Azure AD, Ping, and support generic SAML metadata for other IdPs.
- Session management: configurable session timeouts per customer, token revocation for OIDC refresh tokens, and SAML single logout support (IdP-dependent).

SCIM provisioning
- Endpoints: SCIM 2.0 /Users and /Groups; supports PATCH (RFC 7644), POST, PUT, GET.
- Bulk provisioning: we accept bulk create/update operations via chunked SCIM POST (recommended chunk size configurable; default 500 users). We also support a CSV ingestion helper for partners (we provided an example CSV in the thread).
- Delta handling: We support incremental syncs using 'lastModified' filtering and etag-based conditional requests. Our sync engine writes a per-customer sync cursor so subsequent syncs request only changed resources.
- Conflict resolution: server-side merge rules with last-writer-wins by default; customers can opt into strict attribute-level fail/rollback mode for sensitive attributes (e.g., isAdmin).

RBAC & delegated admin
- Role model: multi-tenant role hierarchy (Tenant Admin, Application Admin, Read-only Auditor, Support Engineer). Roles map to coarse permissions, and fine-grained permission flags are available for enterprise plans.
- Delegated admin: we support scoped delegated admin roles limited to specific namespaces and can bind to SCIM groups or IdP groups to automate membership.
- Admin audit: every role membership change and privilege escalation is logged with actor, timestamp, IP, and before/after deltas. Logs are retained per contract (default 90 days, enterprise options up to 7 years).

Evidence provided here: SCIM architecture diagram, sample sync logs, and a redacted admin audit snippet. Let me know if you want raw log lines rather than the redacted samples.

Elena — great questions. Quick answers and action items below; we've attached the requested sample logs and a suggested delegated admin matrix for your review.

1) SCIM bulk pattern & sync cursor
- Chunked bulk: POST /scim/v2/Bulk with a JSON body of operations; we recommend <=500 ops per chunk. Each successful bulk response includes a X-Redwood-Sync-Cursor header with an opaque cursor string.
- Incremental: subsequent /Users requests can use ?filter=lastModified gt "2027-09-28T00:00:00Z" or include If-None-Match with the last etag returned.
- Retry/dedup: operations carry a client-supplied idempotency_key; server deduplicates matching keys within a configurable window (default 24h).

2) Delegated admin & privilege elevation
- Role matrix attached (admin-role-matrix.xlsx). Delegated roles are scoped and cannot change role definitions; role assignment API is further restricted: only Tenant Admin + MFA-confirmed operator can assign Tenant Admin.
- Elevation protections: we require MFA + approval ticket for elevating to Tenant Admin; elevation events write an audit record and emit a webhook to the customer's security channel. For support engineers we provide just-in-time debug sessions (time-limited, scoped) instead of standing superuser access.

3) Provisioning log sample
- Attached: scim_bulk_sync_logs.csv (CSV for bulk operation IDs) and a redacted JSON lines sample 'user.changed' snippet with fields: event_id, user_id, action, actor, timestamp, changes[]. You can find the full mapping in the linked doc.
